title: feat: filter model catalogs by source and reliability
author: tomdacatto
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #14535

- Adds `source=official|community` and opt-in `reliability=all|reliable` across all eight model-list endpoints, including `/v1/models`. Equivalent `Pollinations-Model-*` headers support client connections; explicit queries take precedence.
- Returns six compact health fields from the existing cached 24-hour feed. Final 4xx responses are excluded; successful fallback rescues count once. Unknown/stale models are excluded by reliable filtering.
- Isolates discovery in one catalog helper. Default payloads, generation access/routing and billing remain unchanged. Detailed monitoring stays on the status endpoints; no database or Tinybird deployment changes.
- Incorporates schema-based header documentation from @ismailbanouigu (#14810) and adapted OpenAI/AI SDK integration coverage from @harisrehman155 (#14570), with co-author credits.

Validation: 25 focused tests passed (catalog/retrieve, OpenAPI, community access and two-client integration), Gen TypeScript, Biome 2.3.10 and diff checks passed. A broader local run encountered a missing Enter OAuth dependency; no full-suite claim.

gist.headline: A catalog with a pulse
gist.blurb: Model lists can now sort the well-tended flowers from the community garden. Ask for official or community sources, then opt into reliable models when you need the path with fewer surprises.
gist.summary: All eight model-list endpoints, including /v1/models, now support source=official|community and opt-in reliability=all|reliable filters via query parameters or Pollinations-Model-* headers, with six compact 24-hour health fields included in catalog responses.
gist.impact: Developers can discover official or community models and filter for reliably healthy options without changing generation routing, access, billing, or default catalog payloads.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy model garden organized into two clearly labeled beds—official and community—while Polli, wearing a tiny gardener hat and holding a health-check clipboard, uses a small sieve to select healthy glowing code-flowers. A friendly CRT monitor robot can display compact heart/status indicators, with reliable blooms thriving and unknown or stale plants gently left outside the selected basket.
